newsitem.title: SPAIN: Guatemala government, rebels to sign pact in Spain.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala government, rebels to sign pact in Spain.

text.p: The Guatemalan government will sign an accord with leftist rebels in Madrid on Thursday to integrate them into society as part of a peace agreement which ended Latin America's longest civil war.

The treaty is the last of three to be sealed before the signing of a final peace agreement on December 29 in Guatemala City. The accords put a end to 36 years of hostilies that have claimed more than 100,000 lives, mainly civilians. Another 40,000 have disappeared.
The final accord outlines the social, political and economic mechanisms to reintegrate guerrillas into civilian and political life.

Under the terms of a ceasefire signed in Oslo on December 4, rebel forces of the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (UNRG) were disarmed and concentrated in eight locations in Guatemala, where they will remain until they return to civilian life.
The government and rebels also concluded a pact on constitutional and electoral reform in Stockholm on December 7. The peace agreements took five years to negotiate.
Spain has been supporting the Guatemalan peace process since 1994 along with Norway, Colombia, the United States, Mexico and Venezuela.
